before.label: Microhistory / everyday life
before.description: Italian microstoria reconstructs relations and tests categories through close inquiry; German Alltagsgeschichte studies everyday practices and power. Neither is defined by small places alone, and their intellectual exchanges do not erase their differences.

strands.title: Mexican microhistoria and local readership
strands.focus: González explains local events alongside regional and national pressures, combining documentary records, informal conversations and personal recollection. His claims to typicality and his treatment of uncorroborated memory are methodological choices open to criticism.

strands.title: Archives, informants and editorial collaboration
strands.focus: González’s preface credits Josefina’s archive, his father’s recollections, other informants and Armida’s revisions. These contributions make the local history a collaborative production despite its single-author title page.

after.scope_note: Italian microstoria and German Alltagsgeschichte have distinct origins and aims; scale alone is not membership in either project. Evidence, narrative and generalization remain contested within this umbrella. Kracauer is a retrospective comparison, not a claimed founder. González’s Mexican microhistoria is included as a distinct local-history project; shared terminology does not establish transmission from Italian or German programmes.

outcomes.finding: Revel’s primary scale argument distinguishes changing observation from magnification. González’s preface provides a distinct Mexican local-history project and records its archival, oral and editorial collaboration. Italian/German distinctions and the Kracauer qualification remain intact.
outcomes.research_limit: Revel: complete numbered sections 3–4 and notes 7–14 of the 1996 essay read in public transcription; opening presentation selective, other sections and chapters unread, no scan collation. González: complete preface and edition notes, 1–18, read in a third-edition scan whose colophon dates it February 1979. Page 13 visually checked for collaboration. Substantive revision notes prevent treating this text as identical to 1968. Historical chapters unread; source and representativeness claims remain the author’s. COLMEX confirms original metadata but full-text route presents CAPTCHA. Arias Gómez (2009), selected 317–325, supplies Armida’s full identity and corroborates collaboration and edition distinctions; remainder unread. No Italian/German transmission to González inferred; his own preface names some European local-history resources, so distinct development is not cultural isolation.
